audit_boundary: Manual audit of Critique-origin verified review-issue clusters. Labels are cluster-level paper-readiness judgments from case-table evidence; final paper claims should still be spot-checked against the original paper text.

clusters.label: B
clusters.missing_or_mismatch: component-isolation ablation for graph control module
clusters.claim_anchor: Diff-Shape is built upon the Graph ControllNet (GrCN) architecture, which combines an unconditioned diffusion model (MIDI) with a graph control module for 3D shape conditioning.
clusters.inventory_or_quote: This approach allowed ControlNet to learn a diverse range of conditional models.(Zhang et al., 2023) Inspired by ControlNet, we introduce a novel diffusion model called Diff-Shape, which combines a pre-trained uncondi...
clusters.raw_paper_evidence_checked: yes: searched graph control / GrCN / ablation; graph control is a named method component and no ablation term was found in the paper text.
clusters.counterevidence_checked: yes: no explicit ablation counterevidence found; inventory anchor is partly related-work ControlNet context, so wording should be cautious.
clusters.wording_caution: Phrase as missing component-isolation ablation for the graph control module, not as evidence of poor performance.
clusters.reason: Defensible concern: graph control module is central to Diff-Shape / GrCN, and the paper appears not to isolate it in ablation; however the inventory quote is not an ablation table and partly cites ControlNet context.

clusters.label: A
clusters.missing_or_mismatch: component-isolation ablation for train an acceptance prediction head
clusters.claim_anchor: SpecDec++ proposes an adaptive candidate length mechanism for speculative decoding, where the number of candidate tokens generated per speculation round is dynamically adjusted based on a learned acceptance probabilit...
clusters.inventory_or_quote: We augment the draft model with a trained acceptance prediction head to predict the conditional acceptance probability of the candidate tokens.
clusters.raw_paper_evidence_checked: yes: searched acceptance prediction / candidate length / ablation; acceptance prediction head is central and no ablation term was found.
clusters.counterevidence_checked: yes: no counterevidence for an acceptance-head ablation found.
clusters.reason: Clear review-worthy issue: SpecDec++ attributes adaptive candidate length to a trained acceptance prediction head, but the paper text exposes no ablation isolating that head.

clusters.label: A
clusters.missing_or_mismatch: component-isolation ablation for recurrent neural network
clusters.claim_anchor: ReDrafter is an advanced speculative decoding approach that achieves state-of-the-art speedup for LLM inference.
clusters.inventory_or_quote: Additionally, we incorporate the embeddings of historical tokens as recurrent inputs to the draft head.
clusters.raw_paper_evidence_checked: yes: searched recurrent / RNN / ablation / draft head; ReDrafter names the RNN draft model as one of three gain drivers and reports other ablations, not an RNN-vs-non-RNN isolation.
clusters.counterevidence_checked: yes: ablations found for beam width, dynamic tree attention, and distillation; no explicit recurrent draft model isolation found.
clusters.wording_caution: Phrase as missing isolation of the recurrent draft model among other reported ReDrafter ablations.
clusters.reason: Clear review-worthy issue: the recurrent draft model is a claimed performance driver, while the ablation section appears to omit an isolation of recurrence/RNN draft-model choice.

clusters.label: B

clusters.inventory_or_quote: To address this issue, we propose the \textbf{Lo}cal-\textbf{G}l\textbf{o}bal \textbf{R}epresentation \textbf{A}lignment framework (\abbr), which employs a two-branch encoder—comprising a multi-scale convolutional bra...
clusters.raw_paper_evidence_checked: yes: searched global encoder / fusion / local encoder / ablation; paper has loss ablations and architecture/backbone comparisons but not a clean Global Encoder removal.
clusters.counterevidence_checked: yes: architecture ablation table partially relates to backbone choice, so this should be worded narrowly rather than as no architecture ablation at all.
clusters.wording_caution: Use cautious wording: missing clean component-isolation ablation for Global Encoder within LogoRA, not missing all architecture experiments.
clusters.reason: Defensible concern: LogoRA claims a local/global/fusion architecture, and current ablations appear to cover losses/backbones rather than isolating the Global Encoder contribution directly.

clusters.label: B
clusters.missing_or_mismatch: runtime, memory, parameter, FLOP, hardware, or compute-cost measurement for the efficiency claim
clusters.claim_anchor: The method is computationally efficient, requiring only a few hundred local distillation steps, and is more efficient than other bi-level dataset distillation methods.
clusters.inventory_or_quote: Despite Federated Learning (FL)'s trend for learning machine learning models in a distributed manner, it is susceptible to performance drops when training on heterogeneous data.
clusters.raw_paper_evidence_checked: yes: searched efficiency / runtime / memory / FLOP / hardware / steps; paper supports efficiency mainly by few-hundred distillation steps and comparison to bi-level methods, with no wall-clock/hardware resource measurement found.
clusters.counterevidence_checked: yes: step-count evidence exists and should be acknowledged; no runtime/memory/hardware counterevidence found.
clusters.wording_caution: Phrase as missing wall-clock/hardware/resource quantification for the efficiency claim, not as no efficiency evidence.
clusters.reason: Defensible efficiency-review concern: the paper makes an efficiency claim, but appears to lack wall-clock/hardware/resource measurements. The original inventory anchor was weak, so wording must acknowledge step-count evidence.

clusters.label: A
clusters.missing_or_mismatch: component-isolation ablation for with a generalized noise regularization
clusters.claim_anchor: The proposed NR-DCCA method introduces a noise regularization mechanism to prevent model collapse in DCCA.
clusters.inventory_or_quote: Therefore, this paper develops NR-DCCA, a DCCA-based method equipped with a generalized noise regularization (NR) approach.
clusters.raw_paper_evidence_checked: yes: searched noise regularization / NR-DCCA / model collapse / ablation; noise regularization is core and no ablation term was found.
clusters.counterevidence_checked: yes: no explicit ablation counterevidence found; theoretical analysis exists but does not replace component-isolation ablation.
clusters.wording_caution: Strong missing-ablation issue; acknowledge theory separately from empirical component isolation.
clusters.reason: Clear review-worthy issue: NR-DCCA centers on generalized noise regularization to prevent model collapse, but the paper text does not appear to isolate that regularizer in ablation.
